hints: Focus on the deep dips (low transmittance) in the spectrum, each strong dip means that bond is absorbing infrared strongly.
Notice the very strong, sharp dip just below 1750 cm-1 and the other very strong dip near 1150 cm-1, then check the table for what bonds absorb there.
Check for what is missing, especially any broad dip above 3200 cm-1 for O-H and any dip near 2200 cm-1 for C triple N, to narrow to one functional group.
walkthrough:
**Spot the three key absorptions**

Look for dips where transmittance falls close to 0%. There are three very strong ones: around 2950 cm-1, around 1450 cm-1 to 1740 cm-1 region, and around 1150 cm-1.

Remember: dip down = absorption.

**Assign C-H, C=O and C-O**

Match each to the data table. The dip at 2850-2950 cm-1 is $\text{C-H}$ (alkane). The very strong sharp dip at about 1740 cm-1 fits $\text{C=O}$ for an ester:
$$1710-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ for ester C=O}$$
The very strong dip at about 1150 cm-1 fits $\text{C-O}$:
$$1040-1300 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ for C-O}$$

**Rule out O-H and C triple N**

There is no broad strong absorption at 2500-3000 cm-1 for carboxyl $\text{O-H}$, and no broad absorption at 3200-3600 cm-1 for hydroxy $\text{O-H}$. There is also no absorption at 2200-2250 cm-1 for $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$.

The combination of $\text{C=O}$ plus $\text{C-O}$ with no $\text{O-H}$ points clearly to an ester.

options.A: An alcohol needs a broad O-H absorption at 3200-3600 cm-1 and a C-O absorption at 1040-1300 cm-1. The spectrum has C-O but lacks the broad hydroxy O-H dip, the small sharp dip near 3500 cm-1 is too weak and sharp to be an alcohol.
options.B: A carboxylic acid needs C=O at 1670-1740 cm-1 plus a very broad O-H absorption over 2500-3000 cm-1 overlapping the C-H region. The spectrum shows sharp C-H peaks, not a broad carboxyl O-H hump, so this is ruled out.
options.C: An ester fits perfectly: strong C=O at 1710-1750 cm-1 (observed near 1740 cm-1) plus strong C-O at 1040-1300 cm-1 (observed near 1150 cm-1), with alkane C-H at 2850-2950 cm-1 and no O-H or C triple N absorption.
options.D: A nitrile requires a characteristic C triple N absorption at 2200-2250 cm-1. The spectrum is flat near 2200 cm-1 with transmittance near 100%, so no nitrile is present.
